# iCode

> iCode builds an open-source agent development environment. iCode Workbench runs a fleet of CLI coding agents in parallel, each in its own isolated Git worktree, and keeps a person in the review loop. iCode Agent is a terminal coding agent that manages its context window on long tasks.

## Products

- [iCode Workbench](${site_origin}/workbench/): run 44 CLI agents in parallel, queue durable tasks, review changes where the agent worked, and keep terminals alive across app restarts. Mira is the cross-project assistant that reads the real queue and tells you what needs you.
- [iCode Agent](${site_origin}/agent/): a terminal coding agent that explores, edits, runs tests, and verifies its own work while defending its context budget.
- [Get started](${site_origin}/get-started/): install iCode Workbench or iCode Agent.
- [FAQ](${site_origin}/faq/): supported platforms, licenses, harnesses, and workflow questions.

## Facts

- iCode Workbench supports 44 CLI coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. 21 harnesses have managed status hooks.
- Every session gets its own Git worktree and branch, so two agents in the same repository never edit the same checkout.
- Tasks are durable and supervised, not autonomous: a permission prompt still waits for a person, and a review decision is separate from process exit.
- Mira is a cross-project assistant. She reads real projects, tasks, sessions, diffs, and review state; she has no shell and cannot approve, merge, push, or edit project code.
- iCode Workbench is licensed AGPL-3.0. iCode Agent is licensed Apache-2.0.
- iCode Workbench runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
